summary: Our project, "Yörük & Çınga: Traces on Mars," is an educational 7-page interactive comic book designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. To address the challenge of communicating space exploration history and STEM to youth, we bridged Mediterranean cultural heritage with advanced space engineering.   We introduced the "Smart Çükür" (GeoScanner Pro)—a high-tech transformation of a traditional Anamur agricultural hand-hoe equipped with OLED displays and XRF/LIBS spectral analysis sensors, modeled after real NASA rovers like Opportunity and InSight. The narrative follows young explorer Yörük and his robot assistant Çınga as they analyze Martian geology while honoring silent robotic pioneers.   This project matters because it elevates space literacy through culturally rooted storytelling, demonstrating how local traditions can inspire space tech. Concluding with an interactive educational guide, it empowers young minds to view space hardware not as debris, but as immortal monuments of human curiosity.
details:
1. How does it work and what does it do?

Our project, "Yörük & Çınga: Traces on Mars," is an educational 7-page interactive bilingual (English/Turkish) flip-book comic accompanied by a 3D technology concept and a 25-second cinematic promo video. The narrative follows young explorer Yörük and his robot companion Çınga on Jezero Crater. Equipped with the "Smart Çükür" (GeoScanner Pro)—a high-tech transformation of a traditional Mediterranean agricultural hand-hoe—they scan Martian soil for mineral and subsurface ice traces while revisiting dormant robotic pioneers such as the Opportunity Rover and InSight Lander.

2. What are the benefits & intended impact?

The project bridges regional Mediterranean cultural heritage with advanced space exploration, making complex space history accessible and engaging for primary and middle school students. Beyond space literacy, it promotes gender equality in STEM: our future roadmap includes securing sponsorships to publish this comic as a physical "STEM Coloring Book" and distributing it free of charge to underprivileged young girls to inspire the next generation of female space explorers.

3. What tools, languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Storytelling & Content: NASA Open Data archives (Opportunity distance telemetry, InSight seismic logs, Jezero Crater surface maps).
  • Design & Conceptualization: Digital graphic illustration software, XRF (X-Ray Fluorescence) and LIBS (Laser-Induced Spectroscopy) sensor schematics, 3D parametric modeling toolsets.
  • Media & Video Production: Digital audio/video editing suites, AI-assisted video production tools (Veo 3), and Interstellar-inspired orchestral sound design.

4. How creative is the project?

Our creativity stems from the fusion of local heritage and futuristic space technology. Transforming a humble traditional hand-hoe into a sensor-laden spectral analysis scanner ("Smart Çükür") demonstrates that everyday tools and local culture can inspire space exploration. Additionally, the physical Flip-Book / Tumble-Book layout allows seamless two-way reading in two languages, creating an interactive physical experience.

5. What factors did the team consider?

The team evaluated space hardware preservation, educational outreach, age-appropriate pedagogical design, zero-waste physical formats, and social impact. We viewed space hardware not as space debris, but as immortal monuments of human curiosity.
